# Insight on Sensor Tag Battery Life: lessons from the field (summary)

Ulrika Brinmoor presented key findings on sensor tag battery life critical to the cold-chain logistics of temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals. Drawing from analysis of over 3,000 multi-day international shipments, she highlighted challenges and best practices to ensure continuous environmental monitoring during transit. Factors affecting battery longevity included wireless communication patterns, sampling frequency, and harsh environmental conditions. Ulrika also discussed new protocols and ongoing developments aimed at extending battery life and improving data reliability.

- Sensor tag battery life should exceed maximum expected transit time by at least 40% to cover delays.
- Wireless transmission intervals must be optimized to reduce battery drain caused by repeated retries in poor network coverage areas.
- Sampling every 15 minutes balances data detail with battery conservation for vaccine shipments.
- Ruggedized sensor tags with enhanced sealing and insulation perform better in extreme humidity and temperature.
- Pre-shipment battery capacity checks within 48 hours of loading prevent failures due to low battery health.

Overall, the session emphasized the importance of tailored sensor tag configurations and proactive maintenance to maintain shipment integrity in complex, multi-day cold-chain routes. Ulrika also previewed plans for smart sensor tags that adapt operations dynamically based on environmental conditions.
